destinations.title: How does a hot brane produce KK gravitons?
destinations.question: Can a hot Standard Model brane gravitationally produce the KK-graviton abundance needed in the Dark Dimension setting, for specified initial brane temperature and bulk population?
destinations.summary: A hot Standard Model brane can populate a KK-graviton tower in the specified scenario. The initial abundance question is separate from whether the population survives as dark matter.

systems: Standard Model brane and KK-graviton tower
regimes: Early-universe hot-brane production in the specified Dark Dimension setup
assumptions: Specified initial brane temperature
Bulk initially essentially unexcited in the arXiv:2311.05318 setup
Gravitational brane coupling
conventions: An initially adequate abundance does not establish viable late-time dark matter
excludes: All gravitational or nonthermal dark-matter production
Independent validation of a fast subsequent cascade
UHECR spectral measurements

destinations.title: How fast can a KK graviton decay near threshold?
destinations.question: How does an intra-tower KK-graviton decay amplitude and rate scale with daughter momentum near threshold, and which background or coupling assumptions control that scaling?
destinations.summary: A supplied 2026 analysis reports a d-wave rate proportional to the fifth power of daughter momentum near threshold. Its derivation and full domain of generality remain outside the reading performed here.

assumptions: Source-specific gravitational action, couplings and background
Generality beyond the supplied setting remains to be checked
conventions: Compare daughter momentum in the parent rest frame
Distinguish amplitude scaling from phase-space-inclusive rate scaling
excludes: A universal theorem for every geometry, field content or higher-derivative theory
Automatic identity of subsequent cosmological conclusions

destinations.title: What do repeated KK decays do to linear structure?
destinations.question: Within the specified repeated-decay KK-graviton model, how do daughter recoil and the changing mass distribution affect linear cosmological perturbations?
destinations.summary: Repeated decays change the tower mass distribution and give daughters recoil velocities. The linear cosmology calculation assumes a specified decay history and does not establish the cascade microphysics.

targets: Recoil constraints and their conditional parameter interpretation
regimes: Source-era CMB, BAO and cosmic-shear analysis
assumptions: Repeated intra-tower decay evolution
Simplified daughter distribution dominated by approximately symmetric decays
Small released mass difference
conventions: The source's kick parameter is a combination of model parameters
Its reported confidence limit is a dated author result
excludes: Nonlinear structure predictions or a demonstrated resolution of the S8 tension
Unconditional viability of the cascade
Visible-energy injection as the primary target

destinations.title: What flat-dimension bounds survive suppressed KK cascades?
destinations.question: In a flat dark dimension with threshold-suppressed KK-graviton cascades, what observational constraints follow from the irreducibly produced population even if it is not all dark matter?
destinations.summary: A flat-dimension analysis argues that unavoidable production and visible decays constrain reheating and radius even when KK gravitons do not constitute all dark matter. Its numerical exclusion remains an attributed result.

systems: KK gravitons in a flat dark dimension
Standard Model brane and visible decay products
regimes: A subdominant KK population is allowed
assumptions: Flat dark dimension
Reported threshold suppression
Specified brane coupling and thermal history
Applicable BBN and CMB reheating floors
conventions: arXiv:2610.01825 uses m_KK=1/R and the four-dimensional reduced Planck mass
Earlier visible-decay constraints use their own mass histories and coupling parameters
excludes: All warped or multidimensional models
An independently checked numerical exclusion curve
Automatic replacement of every earlier conditional phenomenological calculation

readingCoverage.readingLimit: The source reports exclusion of flat radii approximately R≥0.2 micrometres under its assumptions. The calculation, exclusion figure and adopted reheating bounds are outside the supplied window. Comparison sources do not establish that exclusion independently.

methods: Production and decay accounting combined with observational bounds

destinations.title: How do early matter domination and dilution change relic abundance?
destinations.question: How do production timing and entropy release in specified early matter- or modulus-dominated histories determine dark-matter abundance and allowed duration, subject to the relevant reheating, inflationary and dark-radiation constraints?
destinations.summary: Production and dilution can impose competing constraints on an early matter-dominated history. Superheavy neutralinos provide a two-stage example; different relics retain their own channels and expansion histories.

systems: Dark-matter relics and a dominant matter-like field or modulus
targets: Allowed duration of early matter domination
Competition between dilution requirements and inflationary bounds
regimes: Source-specific early matter or modulus domination
Production before domination, during its adiabatic stage or through decay, as specified separately
assumptions: A specified expansion and reheating history
Production channels, branching fractions and sector temperatures remain model-specific
conventions: arXiv:1808.02659's comparison cross section is 3×10^−26 cm^3 s^−1
The EDGES interpretation in arXiv:1812.11915 remains a paper-specific premise
A sufficiently long dilution phase is not by itself a sufficient condition for full viability
includes: BBN reheating floors as boundary inputs
excludes: Scalar-tensor expansion changes automatically identified with entropy dilution
A universal relic formula or duration bound
Current validation of historical anomaly interpretations

readingCoverage.readingLimit: Only arXiv:2010.03573 supplies excerpts for this card. They support the two-stage history, branching-condition statement and opposing duration constraints, but not the complete numerical solution or model scan. Other contributions are description-level.

destinations.title: When do portal interactions produce constrained dark radiation?
destinations.question: How does energy transfer through specified portals populate light hidden species at BBN or recombination, and under which mediator and thermal-history assumptions can radiation bounds be estimated without detailed hidden-sector information?
destinations.summary: Portal interactions can transfer energy into light hidden species. Estimates that are insensitive to hidden-sector details still require explicit mediator and thermal-history assumptions.

systems: Light hidden species and visible plasma
Mirror photons, minicharged fermions and hidden photons in their respective models
Massive SM-singlet mediator models in arXiv:2206.13530
regimes: Equilibrium, partial thermalization and out-of-equilibrium production
assumptions: Portal and initial sector temperatures specified per model
arXiv:2206.13530's generic estimate assumes preferential mediator energy transfer into the hidden sector
Its stated early-history insensitivity requires reheating above the mediator mass
conventions: arXiv:1303.5379 uses Δg*; no unprovided conversion to other radiation parameters is imposed
arXiv:2206.13530 focuses on mediator masses above 0.1 MeV
Exact and broken mirror parity remain separate cases
excludes: A universal mediator-independent bound
Relic matter abundance identified with radiation density
An implicit connector to the Standard Model in an otherwise secluded model

destinations.title: What did historical cosmic-ray spectra show about suppression?
destinations.question: Do the supplied historical Auger and HiRes spectra exhibit a high-energy suppression relative to an unbroken power law, and how are the cutoff or suppression energy, uncertainties and GZK interpretation defined?
destinations.summary: Historical Auger and HiRes spectra provide separate measurements of high-energy suppression. Suppression consistent with GZK expectations does not uniquely identify its cause or establish a gravitational species scale.

systems: Ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays measured by Auger and HiRes
targets: Cutoff and ankle locations where supplied
regimes: The frozen historical datasets and analyses
assumptions: Experiment-specific calibration and spectral models
The HiRes introduction describes the proton-dominated extragalactic premise of the GZK prediction
conventions: Auger's suppression energy is defined by a 50% deficit relative to an extrapolated power law
Do not identify that definition automatically with HiRes's reported cutoff
Statistical significance of suppression differs from confidence in its physical cause
includes: Reported rejection of a single power law
excludes: KK-graviton abundance or decay calculations
A measured dark-dimension species scale
Current cosmic-ray data or a unique mechanism determination

readingCoverage.readingLimit: Auger's supplied analysis passage reports the power-law rejection and its suppression-energy definition. HiRes's significance and feature locations are reported in its abstract; its statistical calculation was not read. Neither excerpt determines a unique suppression mechanism.

destinations.title: How does electroweak symmetry breaking change ALP misalignment?
destinations.question: How does an additional ALP mass generated by an explicit shift-symmetry-breaking Higgs portal at electroweak symmetry breaking modify misalignment evolution and relic-density correlations, depending on when oscillations begin?
destinations.summary: An electroweak Higgs-portal contribution changes the ALP mass without moving the potential minimum in the supplied setup. The relative timing of oscillation onset and electroweak symmetry breaking must remain explicit.

systems: A misaligned ALP and the Standard Model Higgs
regimes: Oscillation onset relative to electroweak symmetry breaking, retaining the introductory before/after and before/at descriptions
assumptions: An existing mass plus an electroweak contribution
The proposed mechanism leaves the potential minimum unchanged
The displayed initial setup is homogeneous with zero initial angular velocity
conventions: The supplied introductory timing descriptions do not substitute for the unprovided case analysis
includes: Modification of conventional misalignment by the electroweak mass contribution
excludes: Identity with kinetic misalignment, monodromy or vector Higgs production
Verified numerical viability regions
